extracted.intended_audience: Researchers serving as peer reviewers for PCI Evolutionary Biology (invited reviewers/recommenders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for researchers performing peer review of preprints submitted to PCI Evolutionary Biology, covering submission requirements, reviewer conduct, evaluation checkpoints for article sections, reproducibility and transparency rules, timelines, and handling of conflicts and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Evolutionary Biology will evaluate preprints dealing with all fields of Evolutionary Biology (list of subjects provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preprints may be empirical or theoretical, based on experiments, observations, previously acquired data, models, or methodology studies; perspectives, reviews, opinions and comments are welcome. The recommender determines whether a preprint is interesting enough to be reviewed; reviewers do not need to assess scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of articles accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: The articles recommended may have diverse formats: reviews, comments, opinion papers, research articles, data papers, technical notes, computer notes, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No editing/formatting/proofs required; authors of recommended articles are asked to add a sentence to acknowledgements stating recommendation by PCI Evolutionary Biology. Anonymous submissions are welcomed; preregistrations should go to PCI RR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation quality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Evolutionary Biology recommends only preprints of high scientific quality that are methodologically and ethically sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommender selects preprints considered interesting; recommendations are intended to draw attention to the qualities of the article including subjective reasons for interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raw data availability (mandatory for recommended articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles recommended by PCI must provide the readers with raw data, made available either in the text or through an open data repository with a DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data must be reusable: metadata and accompanying text must describe the data carefully and accurately; repositories suggested include Zenodo, Dryad, institutional repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and description of quantitative analyses and simulation code (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Details concerning quantitative analyses (data treatment and statistical scripts) and simulations (scripts, codes) must be available in the text or through a correctly versioned deposit in an open repository with a DOI or other permanent identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scripts or codes must be carefully described such that another researcher can reuse them. Note that Git URLs are not permanent; guidance on issuing DOIs for GitHub is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear justification of sample sizes (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear justification of sample sizes for empirical studies must be provided, especially regarding statistical power, Bayes factor thresholds, or estimate precision (quantitative) and information power or saturation thresholds (qualitative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Lakens (2022) for guidance; reviewers should check that sample-size justification is present and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details on experimental procedures (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Details on experimental procedures must be given in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods must be sufficiently detailed to allow replication by other researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of preregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI encourages authors to submit preprints based on preregistrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preregistration clarifies hypotheses and analysis plans and should be submitted to PCI RR; this is a suggested practice rather than mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welcoming replication studies and negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI welcomes reproductions of studies and preprints reporting negative results, provided that the questions addressed and the methodology are sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions are assessed according to the same criteria if the preprint is deemed interesting by the recommender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest policy for submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI does not accept submissions of preprints presenting financial conflicts of interest. Other conflicts must be minimal and declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommenders and referees are expected to declare that they have no conflict of interest with the content or authors; reviewers must certify no conflict prior to accepting an invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent review publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Evolutionary Biology publishes all reviews of recommended manuscripts, with reviewers retaining the right to choose whether to sign their reviews or remain anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and recommender decision letters are published on the PCI platform on recommendation. Reviews of rejected submissions are sent to authors but are not published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of conduct for reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and recommenders are expected to adhere to the PCI code of conduct, avoiding abusive or discriminatory language in their comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews considered to violate the code of conduct may be edited by recommenders or the Managing Board, returned to the reviewer for editing, or discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conflict-of-interest declaration (pre-review)
rubrics_metrics.description: When invited, reviewers must certify that they have no conflict of interest of any kind with the content or with the authors of the preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure about a potential conflict, reviewers should ask PCI managers via contact email; if a conflict exists, they must decline the invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are expected to write their review within three weeks after accepting the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promptly accept or decline invitations to keep time-to-decision short; inform recommender/managers if you anticipate delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommender decision timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the various reviews obtained, the recommender must come to a decision within about 10 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommender may ask authors to revise and may solicit further reviews of revised versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number and quality of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommender invites reviewers to obtain at least two high-quality reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommender and reviewers must declare no conflicts of interest; recommenders handle evaluation initiation and invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process for authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of rejected manuscripts can appeal the PCI decision within 30 days of receiving it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals will be considered by the specialist recommender(s) handling the manuscript and the PCI Evolutionary Biology Managing Board; decisions following appeal are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: No word limits or specific formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PCI Evolutionary Biology imposes no word limits or specific formatting requirements on submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should be as concise as possible but as long as necessary to ensure clarity and reproducibility; authors intending journal submission should note journal-specific limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: General reviewer tone and approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Be constructive, kind, and respectful; be precise and clear; remain open to new approaches; state lack of expertise on certain points; only agree to review manuscripts you can assess in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These guidelines derive from COPE and other peer-review guidance; maintain professionalism because reviews may be published.

rubrics_metrics.name: What reviewers should NOT do
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not have a conflict of interest; you do not need to determine whether the article falls within the scope of the PCI; you do not need to check that scripts/code are available; you do not need to comment extensively on typographical errors; you do not need to check for potential plagiarism; you do not need to make recommendations about acceptance or rejection; you do not need to check the format of references; do not discredit negative results; do not ask for new experiments if the study is already well performed and conclusions are clear; avoid unconstructive, ambiguous, and unsupported comments; you must absolutely not use AI to generate your reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI may be used to translate, correct and improve texts, but not to generate review content. If you have a conflict you must decline. Manuscript scope is considered validated by the Managing Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: What reviewers should DO
rubrics_metrics.description: Promptly accept or decline invitations; try to keep to deadlines; check for conflicts of interest; provide a detailed, objective report on the merits; identify flaws in design, analysis and interpretation; expose concerns about ethics or misconduct; state the preprint's strengths and weaknesses; consider both technical merit and scientific significance; report if something critically missing; provide specific suggestions for improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the core responsibilities of a reviewer whose report may be published and used by the recommender in deciding recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the title clearly reflects the content of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, accurate title helps readers and indexing; mention if title is misleading or incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the abstract is concise and presents the main findings of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend revisions if abstract omits key results or overstates conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the introduction clearly explains the motivation for the study and that the research question/hypothesis/prediction is clearly presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the introduction builds on relevant recent and past research performed in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materials and methods evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that sufficient details are provided for the methods and analysis to allow replication by other researchers and that statistical analyses are appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that experimental procedures, data treatment, scripts, and pipelines are described; ensure sample-size justification is provided where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results evaluation and reproducibility checks
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible, evaluate the consistency of raw data and scripts; if necessary and if you can, run the data transformations and statistical analyses and check that you get the same results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the case of negative results, check that there is a statistical power analysis or an adequate Bayesian analysis; inform the recommender and Managing Board if you suspect scientific misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and figures evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that figures and tables are understandable without reference to the main body of the article and that they have a proper caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each figure/table should be interpretable on its own; flag missing or unclear legends and insufficient labelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the conclusions are adequately supported by the results and that the interpretation of the analysis is not overstated and that the discussion takes account of relevant recent and past research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag overclaims, unsupported extrapolations, or missing consideration of key literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: References evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that all references are appropriate and that the necessary references are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report any reference cited in the text that does not appear in the reference list and highlight missing seminal or recent relevant work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing revised manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how the authors addressed your comments; if you have new requests for modifications, please state them clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In general, try not to start new lines of interrogation if the previous points were addressed adequately; if you disagree with other reviewers and agree with authors' explanations, help the recommender by discussing these issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review anonymity choice
rubrics_metrics.description: When uploading your review you can indicate whether or not you wish to remain anonymous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers retain the option to sign or remain anonymous; consider implications because reviews may be published for recommended papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of editorial correspondence depending on outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recommender decides to reject the article, your review(s) will NOT be published; if the article is recommended, all editorial correspondence (decisions, authors' replies, all reviews) will be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be mindful that their reviews may be made public in the recommended case and adhere to the code of conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics approvals for research involving humans/animals
rubrics_metrics.description: In fields in which research requires approval from an ethics committee or institutional review board, the authors should generally ensure that the proposed research has received all necessary approvals before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should flag missing or inadequate ethical approval statements or concerns about ethical compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data/materials transparency requirement at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, authors are required to make all study data, digital materials, and computer code publicly available (at submission) to the maximum extent permissible by legal or ethical restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers do not need to check that scripts are available (this is a submission prerequisite) but may evaluate reproducibility where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling timeline for unclaimed submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If no recommender has initiated evaluation of the preprint after 20 days, the authors are notified and suggested to cancel their submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This informs authors and limits indefinite waiting; reviewers are not responsible for this monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data permanence and repository guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use open repositories with a DOI or another permanent identifier; Git URLs are not permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Zenodo, Dryad, institutional repositories; information on issuing a DOI for a GitHub repository is provided in the guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scripts/code documentation standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Scripts or codes must be carefully described such that another researcher can reuse them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include versioning and sufficient documentation; reviewers should flag undocumented code or irreproducible pipelines when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI use restriction for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: You must absolutely not use AI to generate your reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you use AI to generate reviews you risk having your text rejected and being banned from PCI; you may use AI to translate, correct and improve your texts only.
